result.title: RealCompanion: Benchmarking Human Understanding from Reasoning over Longitudinal Real-World Conversations
result.summary: A companion that talks with a person for months should come to understand them. It should remember what they said, infer who they are, and know when the past bears on the message in front of it. Testing this requires a real person's record, and such records are private, so benchmarks generate the person and the questions and settle in advance what matters. We release \bench, ten real relationships with an AI companion: 27,218 messages over up to 120 days, released as the conversation and four files derived from it, a profile, a persona, a chat ground truth and a question set, each citing the messages it rests on. Every chat label carries the reasoning trace that produced it, checked stage by stage against the conversation. Three findings follow. First, the past is rarely needed and far away. Pooled measures mislead: a recency window finds the required message for 95.9\% of probes and 2.2\% of those that need memory, and at the natural rate 96\% of the gain from supplying recorded evidence comes from messages that need none. Second, no detector we tried can tell when memory is needed on real messages, authored questions over the same histories leak the cue, and labeling the same messages as memories raises their use by ten to fourteen points. Third, three agent systems reconstruct the persona with the same F1 at a 31-fold difference in cost.

AI.brief_summary: 该文发布 RealCompanion 基准，基于 10 段真实人机伴侣关系、最长 120 天的 2.7 万余条消息，构建画像、人格、对话标注与带推理轨迹的问答集，并给出三个关于「何时需要记忆」的诊断发现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「过去何时与当前消息相关」的判定、推理轨迹标注与供给证据的增益归因，与 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的触发与信息贡献分配问题有具体联系，可供核查长程证据筛选与监督信号设计。
